Need the Wikipedia minimum perigee and Kipchoge’s record marathon pace; I’ll retrieve both from authoritative pages, then calculate and round to the nearest 1000 hours.
I’ll first check the available knowledge documents for these exact facts before using the public web.

Searching the knowledge base for the relevant Wikipedia facts.

```python
knowledge_lookup = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Eliud Kipchoge record marathon pace Moon minimum perigee Wikipedia", scope="session")
print(knowledge_lookup)
```
The knowledge search did not provide the needed source values, so I’ll query Wikipedia directly for the Moon’s minimum perigee and Kipchoge’s record time.
```python
wikipedia_results = await wikipedia_search("Moon Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record", max_results=10)
print(wikipedia_results)
```
I’ll fetch the relevant Wikipedia pages to obtain the exact figures and wording needed for the calculation.
```python
moon_search = await wikipedia_search("Moon", max_results=5)
print(moon_search)
```
I’ll use a targeted web search to locate the exact Wikipedia entries and values if the article search results are insufficient.
```python
targeted_search = await web_search("site:en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon minimum perigee km closest approach", max_results=5)
print(targeted_search)
```
I’ll fetch the Wikipedia Moon article directly, then extract the minimum perigee value from its returned text.
```python
moon_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon", max_chars=30000)
print(moon_page)
```
Now fetching Eliud Kipchoge’s Wikipedia article for the record marathon time.
```python
kipchoge_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge", max_chars=20000)
print(kipchoge_page)
```
Using the Wikipedia figures (minimum perigee 356400 km and marathon world record 2:01:09), I’ll calculate the travel time in hours and round it to the nearest 1000 hours.
```python
calculation = await calculator("(356400 / (42.195 / (2 + 1/60 + 9/3600)))")
print(calculation)
```
17000 hours
